output.summary: An annual to biennial mustard native to Eurasia, Brassica rapa includes cultivated forms such as turnips, bok choy and napa cabbage. Wild and weedy forms typically have a slender taproot and leafy rosette, while turnip forms develop a swollen storage root; most flowers have four yellow petals followed by narrow seed pods. Cultivated varieties are eaten as roots or leafy vegetables, with young leaves eaten raw and older leaves typically cooked.
output.edibilityNote: Cultivated roots and leafy vegetables are eaten; young leaves may be raw, older leaves are typically cooked, and raw seeds may irritate some people.
